blurb:
Monica is one year old, about 35 pounds, and her whole personality can be summed up in one sentence from her listing: her main job in life is to love you as much as possible and spend all her time with you. That's not rescue-flyer language. That's just what she's like.

She came in from animal control a little underweight and is currently going through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so she's picking up real skills while she waits. She's already shown she can make dog friends, and volunteers think a calm, good-natured dog in her new home would actually help her a lot since she deals with some separation anxiety when left alone.

That separation anxiety is worth knowing about upfront. Monica needs a home where someone is around most of the time, a work-from-home situation or a household where she's not sitting alone for long stretches. If that's your setup, she's going to thrive. Mostly Mutts has a trainer ready to help you work through it. She's also heartworm positive right now, but treatment is coming and they're asking for local adoption only so they can stay involved in her care. Kids 15 and up are probably the better fit. Call 770-272-6888 to find out when she's available to meet.
shelter_hours: Please call or visit mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Heartworm-positive status and local-only restriction are meaningful barriers that make newsletter reach disproportionately important for her placement
• 'Her main job is to love you' is quotable, emotionally direct copy that translates instantly to newsletter readers
• Active training program placement suggests she's been waiting long enough to need structured enrichment — moderate urgency with a clear, work-from-home adopter target

blurb:
Rae came into Mostly Mutts from a neglectful situation, along with three other dogs, and has spent the last stretch of time getting the vet care she needed and settling into a foster home. She's 10 years old, about 9 pounds, and she has figured out exactly how she wants to spend her days: some napping, a little exploring, collecting pets from whoever's around, and then more napping. Honestly, goals.

She's not a lap dog and won't demand to be on you constantly, but she's friendly and sweet and appreciates the attention when it comes. She gets along fine with other dogs in her foster home, mostly by ignoring them, so if you have a calm dog who's not looking for a wrestling buddy, she'll fit right in. Cats are unknown.

One thing to know: Rae is hard of hearing. Regular voice commands don't land as well, but her foster gets her attention by tapping her leg, and she comes right over. It's a small adjustment, not a big deal. Mostly Mutts offers free lifetime training classes with every adoption, and they're happy to help you figure out what works for her. She'd do best with older kids who know how to be gentle with a small, senior dog. She recently had a spay, dental work, and a mammary mass removal, and she's healing up well. If you want a quiet, low-key companion who just needs a soft place to land, Rae is worth a visit.
shelter_hours: Please call or visit mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Senior dog rescued from neglect, fresh out of surgery, and hard of hearing — the combination of vulnerability and resilience is the most emotionally rich story in this set
• Her low-maintenance lifestyle and 'soft place to land' framing is a direct pitch to older or quieter households who are underserved by typical adoption content
• Age, medical history, and neglect origins all point to an extended shelter journey — highest urgency of the group and the clearest case for featured placement

blurb:
Josie came from animal control, got rescued by Mostly Mutts, went through their Prison Pups training program, got adopted, came back because her energy was too much for that family, and is now in a foster home waiting for someone who actually wants a dog with some life in her. That's a lot of plot twists for a 6-year-old hound mix who weighs 35 pounds and has the most ridiculous floppy ears you've ever seen.

She knows sit, stay, and how to be genuinely sweet with people. She'll go on a walk with you and then fold herself onto the couch afterward. Energy level is a 5-7 with occasional zoomies, which is basically the description of a fun dog, not a problem dog. The training she did through Prison Pups means she actually has some manners to build on.

Here's what Josie needs in a home: she's got to be your only pet. No other dogs, no cats. She's had trouble making dog friends, and the cat situation was a hard no. Kids 10 and older are probably a good fit since she can get mouthy during play, but volunteers describe it as playful nibbling, never aggressive. If you've got an active household without other animals, call her name.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can reach them at 770-272-6888 to find out more about meeting Josie.
shelter_hours: Please call or visit mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Return adoption after a failed placement is the most compelling narrative in this batch — readers root for a second-chance dog
• Prison Pups training plus real manners makes her a standout candidate who just needs the right-fit home, not more work
• Multiple system touchpoints — animal control, rescue, training program, adoption, return, foster — signal a long road that demands urgent newsletter spotlight

blurb:
Dionne came into Mostly Mutts through animal control with her sister, spent time in a foster home, and then came back to the shelter where the volunteers have apparently been spoiling her ever since. She's three months old, about four and a half pounds, and fully litter trained.

Her personality is pretty straightforward: curious, playful, loves kitten toys, and recharges from nap to chaos and back again on a pretty reliable cycle. She gets along well with her sister and is comfortable around gentle kids. Dogs are unknown since she hasn't had much exposure there.

One thing worth knowing up front: Dionne isn't spayed yet because she's still too small. Mostly Mutts requires it and will cover the cost once she's big enough, but the procedure has to be done through one of their approved vets in North Metro Atlanta. So this one is local adoptions only. Adoption fee is $175. If that works for you, she's ready to meet you. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw.
shelter_address: 2875 George Busbee Pkwy NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144
shelter_hours: Check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• Local-only restriction and pending spay requirement are real friction points that make newsletter visibility especially valuable for moving her
• Volunteer-spoiled shelter kitten with a reliable chaos-nap cycle is an easy, charming visual for readers
• Back at the shelter after foster care suggests she's been in the system longer than her age implies — modest urgency worth noting

blurb:
Rice is the quiet one. Her siblings came in from animal control together, spent time in a foster home, and are now ready to find homes. The other two warmed up fast. Rice takes a little longer. She's going to sit back and watch you for a minute before she decides what she thinks of you. That's not a problem. That's just who she is.

Here's what the listing says happens once she makes up her mind: you've got a shadow. She won't be more than a foot away from you. She goes from reserved to loyal pretty fast once she trusts you, and at two and a half months old and two and a half pounds, she's got a lot of years of loyalty ahead of her.

She's litter trained, good with kids she's met in foster care, and has had limited exposure to other cats without any issues. Dogs are unknown since she hasn't had much contact. If you're looking for a kitten who earns your bond instead of demanding it from day one, Rice might be your girl. She just moved into the Kitty Room at Mostly Mutts and is ready to meet people. Stop in and give her a few minutes to size you up.
shelter_address: 2875 George Busbee Pkwy NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144
shelter_hours: Check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• 'Earns the bond' narrative gives introverted or patient readers an unusually personal hook to connect with
• Her shadow-loyalty trait is a sleeper-hit story — reserved kitten becomes devoted companion is a compelling arc
• Just moved to the Kitty Room, suggesting she's ready now but the unknown dog compatibility quietly narrows her pool

blurb:
At two and a half months old and barely a pound and a half, Emu showed up at Mostly Mutts after losing her mom at five weeks old. She went straight into a foster home with her siblings and, according to the foster mom, she's been thriving ever since. She's the independent one of the litter, which sounds like a contradiction for a kitten this small, but it just means she brings the full package: playful and running laps when she's got energy, cuddled up in your lap when she's done.

She's already litter trained, loves chasing mouse toys, and has figured out that tunnels are basically the best invention ever. Her foster mom says the whole litter is pretty much perfect, but Emu has a little extra personality. She gets along great with other cats and has handled every dog and kid she's met without much fuss.

If you've got another cat at home who could use a small, athletic, occasionally chaotic roommate, Emu is worth the trip. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Check their website for the adoption process and to schedule a meet.
shelter_address: 2875 George Busbee Pkwy NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144
shelter_hours: Check mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours
scoring_notes:
• Highly adoptable kitten with litter training, multi-pet compatibility, and a bold personality that writes its own headline
• Foster-home success story gives readers immediate confidence this kitten is healthy and socialized
• Recently placed and thriving — low urgency, but strong feel-good feature for a family-friendly issue
